name: Great Pyramids of Giza & Great Sphinx
description: The oldest and only surviving monument of the original Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
history: Constructed over 4,500 years ago during Egypt's Fourth Dynasty, the Great Pyramid of Giza was built as a monumental tomb for Pharaoh Khufu. For over 3,800 years, it was the tallest man-made structure in the world.
construction: Composed of an estimated 2.3 million limestone and granite blocks weighing an average of 2.5 tons each, precisely aligned to true north with an error of less than one-tenth of a degree.
architecture: Features sophisticated internal corbelled chambers including the Grand Gallery, Queen's Chamber, and King's Chamber, surrounded by the mortuary complex and the colossal Great Sphinx.
significance: Designated an original Wonder of the Ancient World in the 2nd century BCE by Antipater of Sidon and Philo of Byzantium. Awarded permanent Honorary Wonder Status in the 2007 New 7 Wonders declaration.
currentStatus: Standing intact and protected as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1979.
wonderDesignationYear: c. 225 BCE (Antipater of Sidon Canon) & July 7, 2007 (Honorary Wonder)
wonderReplacedBy: Retained timeless honorary supremacy in the New 7 Wonders declaration
wonderHistoricalContext: Constructed c. 2560 BCE for Pharaoh Khufu, the Great Pyramid was the first and oldest of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. In 2007, when the New 7 Wonders campaign concluded in Lisbon, Giza was granted unique permanent Honorary Status, as it was the sole surviving monument from the original ancient canon.
